digest.top_line: TREASURE: consolidative TRT after chemo-IO in ES-SCLC halted for excess fatal SAEs, mOS 6.7 vs 13.4mo (HR 1.55) and SAEs 61.3% vs 18.2%.
digest.tldr: Thoracic carried the day, and it is a negative safety signal, not an efficacy one: adding 30 Gy/10 fx to atezolizumab maintenance tripled SAEs and killed 19.4% of pts, with no dosimetric or timing explanation and near-universal post-TRT lymphopenia. The control arm outperformed IMpower133, so the deficit sits with TRT plus ongoing IO, not a weak comparator.

sites.intro: Consolidative TRT layered onto continuing checkpoint blockade in ES-SCLC is the question, and the SMC answered it before the trial finished accruing.

studies.name: Consolidative Thoracic RT + Atezolizumab Maintenance (ES-SCLC)
studies.tldr: mOS 6.7 vs 13.4mo (HR 1.55, P=.34) and SAEs 61.3% vs 18.2% with consolidative TRT; trial halted early.

details: 📊 TRT associated with AE risk over time (HR 2.47, 95% CI 1.15-5.32, P = .01); atezolizumab exposure was not (HR 0.57, 0.30-1.08, P = .06)
📊 Lymphopenia after TRT: cycle 2 ALC <0.001/μL in 22/24 (91.7%) arm A vs 3/22 (13.6%) arm B, P < .001; leukocytes and neutrophils unaffected
📐 Fatal-AE pts in arm A had worse baseline DLCO SB (45.3 [13.7] vs 56.7 [11.4], P = .04)
🔗 Arm B mOS 13.4mo and 1-y OS 56.6% exceed the IMpower133 atezolizumab arm (12.3mo, 51.7%); arm A fell below it
🔗 Directionally consistent with PACIFIC-2 and CheckMate-73L, where simultaneous thoracic chemoRT + IO in NSCLC also produced more fatal infections

verdict.rationale: Randomised, prespecified OS primary, stopped early for harm; descriptive only after halt, but the toxicity signal is the actionable read, not the underpowered HR.

studies.significance: The PFS/OS dissociation is the RT read: PFS was identical (2.4 vs 2.6 mo, HR 0.92), so 30 Gy/10 fx bought no systemic disease control while OS fell, pointing at toxicity rather than progression. Lymphopenia was TRT-specific and persistent, and timing (concurrent vs sequential) did not rescue it.
studies.monday_clinic: In ES-SCLC with at least stable disease after chemoimmunotherapy, this argues against adding consolidative TRT to atezolizumab maintenance off-trial in unselected pts; it does not address TRT for symptomatic thoracic disease or the limited-stage chemoRT setting.

primary_endpoint.name: Overall survival
primary_endpoint.stat_detail: HR 1.55 (0.90-2.69), P = .34; primary end point not met

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multicenter open-label **phase 2 randomised** trial (TREASURE, AIO-TRK-0320) at 20 sites in Germany and Austria, accrual Sept 2020 to Aug 2022, last follow-up Sept 2024. Planned 104 randomized for 80% power; **halted at 68** on SMC recommendation, so interpretation is descriptive.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: ES-SCLC with **at least stable disease after induction carboplatin-etoposide-atezolizumab**. Thoracic PR in 30 (88.2%) arm A vs 26 (76.5%) arm B; brain mets in 1 pt per arm; PCI in 7 (20.6%) vs 9 (26.5%). Preexisting interstitial lung disease was an exclusion criterion, with central review mandated from April 2021.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **30 Gy in 10 fractions**, target volume delineated on the **postinduction** volume of thoracic primary plus involved nodal metastasis. Doses and volumes were within or below typical clinical ranges and below established OAR thresholds. Randomization stratified by brain metastases, induction response, and PCI.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: overall survival** from randomization. Secondary: PFS, frequency and severity of AEs and SAEs. Stratified log-rank plus multivariable Cox in ITT, with per-protocol and adjusted-ITT (excluding fatal AEs) sensitivity sets.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Toxic effects in 30 (96.8%) arm A vs 25 (75.8%) arm B (P = .02); **trAEs 71.0% vs 30.3%** (P = .001), trSAEs 29.0% vs 6.1% (P = .01). SAEs were dominated by **infections and respiratory disorders**. Grade 3 or greater trAE rate in arm A (26%) exceeds benchmarks for atezolizumab monotherapy and for consolidative TRT without immunotherapy.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Prior prospective **single-arm** studies of TRT added to chemoimmunotherapy reported no toxicity increase; the randomised comparison here does not reproduce that. The pattern matches **PACIFIC-2** and **CheckMate-73L**, where simultaneous thoracic chemoradiotherapy with IO in NSCLC produced more fatal infections and toxic effects in the interventional arms.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents unselected ES-SCLC pts responding to or stable after chemoimmunotherapy, receiving consolidative TRT during atezolizumab maintenance. Does not represent limited-stage SCLC, palliative TRT for symptomatic thoracic disease, or pts selected by pulmonary reserve or lymphocyte kinetics.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The **OS curves crossed at approximately 24 months** with 2-year rates numerically favoring arm A (24.2% vs 15.7%), on very few pts at risk, so the direction of late benefit is unresolvable here. Causal attribution of the fatal events diverged between assessors: investigators called 4 arm A deaths unrelated, the SMC reclassified 3 as possibly or probably related.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The **absence of any PFS difference** (HR 0.92) argues that TRT added no meaningful tumor control, while the OS gap points to treatment-related toxicity as the driver rather than accelerated progression. An adjusted-ITT sensitivity analysis excluding fatal AEs gave consistent OS results, so the arm A disadvantage is not carried by those deaths alone.

studies.interpretation:
The result that should move an RT reader here is not the hazard ratio, which a 68-patient trial stopped for harm cannot settle, but the shape of the discordance between the two survival endpoints. PFS was flat across arms (2.4 vs 2.6 months, HR 0.92) while OS diverged sharply. In a disease where thoracic failure is common and where the original Slotman rationale for consolidative TRT was precisely to convert local control into survival, a null PFS is a strong statement: the 30 Gy in 10 fractions delivered to postinduction volumes did not buy enough disease control to register at the level of the whole-patient progression endpoint. Whatever the OS numbers turn out to be with more patients, an intervention that leaves PFS untouched has very little upside left to trade against its harms.

Those harms are where the trial is most credible, because a randomized comparison is exactly what the prior literature lacked. Single-arm series of TRT added to chemoimmunotherapy reported no toxicity increase, and that reassurance is what carried the practice into use. TREASURE says the reassurance was an artifact of having no control arm: SAEs 61.3% versus 18.2%, fatal events 6 versus 1, and a grade 3 or greater treatment-related AE rate in the combination arm that exceeds published benchmarks for either component alone. The last point matters most, since it is the one observation that cannot be explained by simply adding two toxicity profiles together and instead implies interaction. The convergent signal from PACIFIC-2 and CheckMate-73L, where thoracic radiotherapy delivered simultaneously with checkpoint blockade produced more fatal infections in NSCLC, makes it harder to dismiss this as a small-trial accident.

The proposed mechanism is worth taking seriously precisely because it is testable and because it predicts who is at risk. Lymphocyte depletion after TRT was profound and persistent, specific to lymphocytes rather than a general marrow effect, and tracked with the accumulation of infectious and respiratory events. Reading that alongside the finding that fatal-AE patients had worse baseline DLCO SB gives the outline of a selection strategy rather than a blanket prohibition. What weakens the mechanistic story is the negative dosimetric analysis: no clinical or dosimetric parameter separated patients with and without SAEs, and concurrent versus sequential delivery made no difference either. If lymphopenia is the pathway, one would expect some dose-volume handle on it, and this trial did not find one. That may be a sample-size problem or it may mean the relevant exposure was not among the variables examined.

A skeptic has real material. The trial was halted, so every efficacy comparison is descriptive; the OS confidence interval crosses one; the curves cross at roughly 24 months with two-year rates numerically favoring the radiotherapy arm, on a handful of patients still at risk. But the toxicity comparison does not depend on the trial reaching its planned accrual, and the sensitivity analysis excluding fatal adverse events still showed the arm A disadvantage, which removes the simplest explanation that a few catastrophic deaths dragged the curve down. The defensible read is narrow and specific: in unselected patients responding to chemoimmunotherapy, adding consolidative thoracic radiotherapy during maintenance carries a real toxicity cost with no visible disease-control return, and any future attempt at this question needs a selection criterion and a lymphocyte-sparing plan before it starts.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: PFS was identical across arms (2.4 vs 2.6 mo, HR 0.92), so 30 Gy/10 fx to postinduction volumes bought no measurable disease control while toxicity rose. Doses were below OAR thresholds and concurrent vs sequential timing changed nothing, so replanning does not obviously fix this: the decision it moves is whether to offer consolidative TRT at all during maintenance.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: The comparator arm performed normally (mOS 13.4 mo, 1-y OS 56.6%, above IMpower133's 12.3 mo and 51.7%), so this is a radiotherapy safety signal, not an atezolizumab one. Atezolizumab exposure itself was not associated with AE risk (HR 0.57, P = .06), which keeps maintenance monotherapy intact as the reference strategy.

papers.title: Consolidative Thoracic Radiotherapy With Atezolizumab Maintenance in Extensive-Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer
papers.abstract: Importance Chemoimmunotherapy followed by immunotherapy maintenance is the standard first-line treatment for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC), yet data regarding efficacy and safety of consolidative thoracic radiotherapy (TRT) are lacking. Objective To determine whether combining consolidative TRT with immunotherapy maintenance in ES-SCLC is safe and improves patients’ overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). Design, Settings, and Participants This was a multicenter open-label phase 2 randomized clinical trial recruiting patients from September 2020 to August 2022 in Germany and Austria, with the last follow-up visit in September 2024. Eligible patients had ES-SCLC with at least stable disease after induction chemoimmunotherapy (carboplatin−etoposide−atezolizumab). Although the database was locked in April 2025, a post hoc survival update was performed in April 2026. Data were analyzed from April 2025 to April 2026. Interventions Randomized (1:1) to either atezolizumab maintenance combined with consolidative TRT (30 Gy in 10 fractions) (arm A) or atezolizumab maintenance alone (arm B). Main Outcome and Measure OS (time from randomization to death due to any cause). Results Of 96 patients assessed for eligibility, 68 patients were randomized; recruitment was prematurely terminated due to safety concerns. Median OS in the combination arm was numerically shorter compared to atezolizumab only (6.7 months [95% CI, 5.1-9.0] vs 13.4 months [95% CI, 10.7-17.5]; HR, 1.55 [95% CI, 0.90-2.69]; P = .34), while median PFS was similar (2.4 months [95% CI, 1.3-3.9] vs 2.6 months [95% CI, 1.2-3.9]; HR, 0.92 [95% CI, 0.54-1.55]; P = .85). TRT plus atezolizumab was accompanied by higher frequency of severe adverse events (SAEs) (19 patients [61.3%] vs 6 patients [18.2%]; P &amp;lt; .001) and fatal outcomes (6 patients [19.4%] vs 1 patient [3.0%]; P = .04). Safety analysis revealed predominance of infection and respiratory disorder−related SAEs, possibly facilitated by a depletion of lymphocytes observed specifically in patients after TRT, and by a lower single breath diffuse capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide in patients with fatal AEs in arm A. No further risk factors were identified, given that baseline characteristics were well balanced between both arms and between patients with and without SAEs, including fatal SAEs. Conclusions and Relevance In this randomized clinical trial, TRT combined with immunotherapy increased toxic effects in unselected patients with ES-SCLC without survival benefit, presumably due to radiation-induced lymphocyte depletion facilitating infections. Cautious patient selection and further investigation to identify those who may benefit without undue risk are required. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04462276
